items.title: Closed top-level failed-attempt artifact envelope
items.statement: The schema defines a JSON object titled Runtime Artifact failed_attempts and rejects undeclared top-level properties.

items.title: Required envelope fields
items.statement: A valid artifact must supply schema and artifact discriminators, project/run/attempt identity, creation time, projection freshness and health, retention class, routing references, and a type-specific payload; all other declared fields are optional.

items.title: Fixed schema and artifact discriminators
items.statement: schema_id is fixed to pm.runtime_artifact.failed_attempts.schema.v1 and artifact_type is fixed to failed_attempts, preventing a differently typed artifact from validating under this schema.

items.title: Non-empty identity and routing minimums
items.statement: artifact_id, project_id, run_id, and attempt_id must be non-empty strings; routing_refs must contain at least one non-empty string. The schema therefore carries minimum identity and propagation handles but does not define their resolution behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Identifier syntax, uniqueness scope, referential integrity, and routing resolution are not constrained by this schema.

items.title: Operational metadata lacks semantic constraints
items.statement: created_at_utc, projection_freshness, projection_health, and retention_class are required but constrained only as strings (with created_at_utc merely non-empty). The schema supplies no timestamp format, controlled vocabulary, state relationship, or retention semantics.
items.impact: Producers can emit mutually incompatible freshness, health, time, and retention values that all pass validation, preventing deterministic lifecycle and operational handling.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent timestamp parsing, projection states, health states, and retention-class meanings.

items.title: Failed-attempt payload and lifecycle are undefined
items.statement: The only type-specific requirement is that type_payload be a non-empty object. No failed-attempt reason, classification, terminal or retryable state, retry linkage, recovery action, transition rule, or completion outcome is defined.
items.impact: An artifact can validate without conveying why an attempt failed or how consumers should recover, retry, or close the failure.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must design the complete failed-attempt payload and lifecycle contract.

items.title: Authority, ownership, and consumer obligations are not established
items.statement: producer_ref and actor_ref are optional unconstrained strings, while routing_refs is only a required list of strings. The schema does not say who is authoritative, who owns remediation or retention, which consumers must receive the artifact, or what any referenced party must do.
items.impact: Implementations can disagree about the record of authority, remediation owner, delivery targets, and consumer obligations while remaining schema-valid.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose authority, ownership, routing semantics, and consumer responsibilities.

items.title: Security and privacy rules are absent
items.statement: detail_ref, content_ref, source_surface, producer_ref, actor_ref, and the open type_payload may identify or reference sensitive failure material, but the schema defines no access control, redaction, confidentiality, integrity, provenance-validation, or data-minimization requirements.
items.impact: Sensitive failure content and actor or producer references can be represented without enforceable protection or minimization rules.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent protection and disclosure rules for references and payload content.

items.title: Collection and payload size are unbounded
items.statement: receipt_refs has no maximum item count, routing_refs has a minimum but no maximum, and type_payload has no property or size ceiling. The schema therefore provides no scale or performance bound for artifact validation, transport, storage, or fan-out.
items.impact: Schema-valid artifacts can grow without a declared bound, producing divergent limits or resource exhaustion across implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose collection, payload, transport, and storage limits.

items.title: Version identifier has no compatibility or migration policy
items.statement: The schema and schema_id identify version v1, but this window defines no forward or backward compatibility behavior, unknown-version handling, migration path, or deprecation rule.
items.impact: Consumers cannot determine how to handle artifacts from future or legacy schema versions.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must decide compatibility, rejection, and migration behavior beyond exact v1 validation.

items.title: Structural JSON Schema validation oracle
items.statement: Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validation provides an exact oracle for the declared top-level shape, required fields, discriminator constants, string minimum lengths, array minimums and item shapes, and non-empty type_payload. It is not an oracle for the omitted semantic rules identified in this review.

items.title: Open string and payload semantics create consequential builder discretion
items.statement: Most optional references and descriptive fields are unconstrained strings, and type_payload is an open non-empty object. Identifier formats, reference schemes, payload keys, nullability conventions, text limits, and cross-field invariants are therefore ambiguous.
items.impact: Independent producers and consumers can make incompatible yet schema-valid choices for reference, payload, and cross-field semantics.
items.builder_discretion: All identifier/reference formats, payload structure, string bounds, and cross-field invariants not explicitly declared remain implementation choices.

dimension_assessments.summary: Validation behavior for the closed top-level object, required members, constants, and minimum shapes is explicit.
The schema can validate a structurally typed failed-attempt artifact envelope with identity, operational metadata, routing, references, and a payload.
The accepted JSON artifact input/output shape and its required envelope fields are explicit, although payload semantics remain a gap.
Structural contracts, discriminator constants, required properties, and minimum identity/routing constraints are explicit.
No failed-attempt state model, transition, retryability, terminality, or recovery progression is defined.
Optional producer and actor references do not establish an authoritative record or decision authority.
No remediation, lifecycle, or retention owner is normatively assigned.
Routing references exist, but required consumers and their obligations are undefined.
This JSON artifact schema makes no GUI or user-visible presentation contract.
Despite the failed_attempts discriminator, failure cause, classification, retry, recovery, and closure semantics are absent.
References and open payload content have no access, confidentiality, integrity, redaction, or minimization constraints.
At least one routing reference is required, but resolution, delivery, fan-out, ordering, and acknowledgement behavior are unspecified.
Required freshness, health, retention, and creation metadata lack operational vocabularies and semantics.
Arrays and the open payload have no upper bounds or resource envelope.
The v1 identity is fixed, but compatibility, unknown-version, migration, and deprecation behavior are not defined.
Draft 2020-12 validation is a precise structural oracle for declared constraints, but not for omitted semantics.
Open strings, references, payload structure, and absent cross-field rules leave consequential implementation choices.
Operational vocabularies, failure lifecycle, authority, ownership, consumer behavior, security policy, compatibility, and cross-field semantics remain unknown.
